I changed `preprocess_field_name` in `label_studio/data_manager/functions.py`. It now strips the leading `data.` only once, instead of replacing every `data.` in the string. The Data Manager tests pass: 340 passed, 2 skipped. I didn't add a new test for this change.

This function turns user-supplied filter and ordering column names into Django ORM paths. Its own docstring warns against using `replace` there, because of the earlier ORM Leak issue (#5012), but it still used `replace`. A column like `data.a.data.b` would have been rewritten into `data__a__b`, so a client could change which path got queried. Now only the prefix is converted. A later `data.` stays part of the JSON key name.

This changes behavior for one case: a JSON key path that itself contains `data.` after the prefix is no longer split into extra levels. No existing test relied on the old behavior.

CHOICE: In `preprocess_field_name`, replaced the all-occurrences `.replace('data.', ...)` with a prefix-only `removeprefix`, because the function's docstring forbids `replace` on user-supplied column names (ORM Leak, #5012).
